examples.said: What is, what is called the method that AnkiDroid uses
examples.correct: What's the method AnkiDroid uses called? / What's it called, the method AnkiDroid uses?

items.rule: In "what is X called?", the subject (X) goes between "is" and "called".

examples.said: teach how to run the application
examples.correct: teach them how to run the application / show how to run

items.rule: "teach" normally needs the person: teach someone (how) to do something.
items.notes: Geison flagged this pattern himself during the session.

examples.said: all the known words that I know
examples.correct: all the words I already know

examples.said: store all my known words
examples.correct: store the words I already know

items.rule: Avoid "known words that I know" (redundant); "my known words" sounds unnatural.

examples.said: the most dangerous errors
examples.correct: my most serious / biggest / most common mistakes

items.rule: Mistakes are "serious", "major", or "common", not "dangerous".

examples.said: unnatural ways that I'm talking
examples.correct: the unnatural ways I speak / things I say that sound unnatural

items.rule: Use simple present for habits ("I speak"), not continuous.

examples.said: My pronunciation is not the best one
examples.correct: My pronunciation isn't great / isn't the best

items.rule: Drop "one" when there is no noun being replaced.

examples.said: you found an error ... and then you focus
examples.correct: when you find an error ... you focus on it

items.rule: Describing a general process: use present ("find") consistently.

examples.said: a, a / we, we / at our, at our / that, that / the, the
examples.correct: (pause silently or use um / so)

examples.said: my, to another / could be, this could be / the, the / what's, what's
examples.correct: (pause silently or use um / so)

examples.said: at this, at the exact time / not, not / in a, in a
examples.correct: (pause silently or use um / so)

examples.said: how does your, how does / let's, let's / the, the / you, you
examples.correct: (pause silently or use um / so)

examples.said: an when… / you know
examples.correct: (pause silently)

items.rule: Frequent word repetition while thinking; practice pausing silently or using fillers like "um" / "so".

examples.said: create not lectures, like sessions
examples.correct: create not lectures but practice sessions

items.rule: Use the "not X but Y" structure.

examples.said: words that I don't know their meaning
examples.correct: words whose meaning I don't know / words I don't know

items.rule: Use "whose" instead of "that … their" for possession in relative clauses.

examples.said: words are most fa- famous that I don't know
examples.correct: words are most common that I don't know / the most common words I don't know

items.rule: "Famous" is for people/places; for frequency use "common" / "frequent".

examples.said: words … that I don't know of
examples.correct: words I don't know

items.rule: "Know of" means being aware something exists; for knowing a word's meaning, say "know".

examples.said: change the English repo to private
examples.correct: make the English repo private

items.rule: More natural: "make the repo private" (not "change … to private").

examples.said: Once a day, you create a routine
examples.correct: once a day, run a routine / create a routine that runs once a day

items.rule: You create a routine once; it runs on a schedule (once a day).

examples.said: correct my mistakes at the exact time
examples.correct: correct my mistakes right away / in real time / immediately

items.rule: For correcting during the conversation, prefer "right away" or "in real time" (not "at the exact time").

examples.said: not in a different time
examples.correct: not later / not afterwards

items.rule: Portuguese calque of "em outro momento"; say "not later" instead of "not in a different time".

examples.said: How does a Asian would help to track my pronunciation?
examples.correct: How would Azure help track my pronunciation?

examples.said: How does the pronunciation teaching works?
examples.correct: How does the pronunciation teaching work?

items.rule: One auxiliary per question; after does/would use a base verb (not does+would, not does+works). How would X help…? / How does X work?
items.notes: Lesson 1 (2026-10-19): one auxiliary + base verb — all 3 exercises correct (quality 5).

examples.said: a Asian
examples.correct: Azure (no article before a name)

items.rule: Do not use a/an before proper names.
items.notes: STT wrote Asian for Azure; article error still applies to the intended name.

examples.said: set up the Azure two
examples.correct: set up Azure too

items.rule: Homophone: too (= also), not the number two.

examples.said: the password you can ask me
examples.correct: you can ask me for the password

items.rule: Ask someone for something.

examples.said: I'm thinking of the best way
examples.correct: I'm thinking about the best way

items.rule: Prefer think about when considering a topic or plan.

examples.said: not in a, blah, I have to do this again way
examples.correct: not in a boring, I-have-to-do-this-again way

items.rule: Keep the adjective (boring); hyphenate the attitude phrase if needed.

examples.said: Since you, you have to return, every time I make a mistake
examples.correct: Since you have to answer me every time I make a mistake

items.rule: Return ≠ answer/reply in this context.

examples.said: the ones I repeat the most in the last 90 days
examples.correct: the ones I've repeated the most over the last 90 days

examples.said: what I changed in my routine I started using crockpot alot
examples.correct: One thing I've changed in my routine is that I've started using a crock pot a lot

items.rule: Period up to now → present perfect (I've repeated); often over the last X days.
items.notes: Lesson 3 (2026-10-22): Q1 used has rewritten correctly; Q2 used simple past changed/started (fail).

examples.said: I play the beach tennis tournament a few weeks ago
examples.correct: I played in a beach tennis tournament a few weeks ago

items.rule: Past time marker (a few weeks ago) → past tense: play → played.

examples.said: play the beach tennis tournament
examples.correct: play in a beach tennis tournament

items.rule: Use play in a tournament (not play the tournament).

examples.said: I was out of the field
examples.correct: I was out of practice / I hadn't played in a while

items.rule: Not "out of the field" for sports inactivity; say out of practice / hadn't played in a while.

examples.said: I was idle for a few months
examples.correct: I took a few months off

items.rule: For a break from a sport/activity, prefer took time off / was away from it (idle often sounds like doing nothing at all).

examples.said: Where are we run, are we running in the bot computer?
examples.correct: Where is it running — on the bot computer?

items.rule: Ask where is it running? (present continuous + right subject), not where are we run.

examples.said: Whats taking so long
examples.correct: What's taking so long?

items.rule: What's = what is — needs the apostrophe.

examples.said: in this moment
examples.correct: right now

items.rule: Portuguese calque of "neste momento"; say "right now" (not "in this moment").
items.notes: Native rewrite practiced: "Can you send me a quick lesson right now, just to test it?"

examples.said: a little lesson
examples.correct: a quick lesson

items.rule: For a short on-demand lesson, prefer "a quick lesson" / "a short lesson" over "a little lesson".

examples.said: lesson (heard as less and less)
examples.correct: /ˈlɛsən/ — one word, stress on first syllable

items.rule: Say lesson as one word /ˈlɛsən/ with /ɛ/ (as in "less") and stress on the first syllable — not "less and less".

examples.said: moment (final /t/ dropped)
examples.correct: /ˈmoʊmənt/ with a clear final T

items.rule: Release a clear final /t/ in moment /ˈmoʊmənt/ — don't drop it (heard as /n/).

examples.said: she should have tested before sending, publishing it to production
examples.correct: she should have tested it before pushing it to production

items.rule: Transitive verbs like test usually need an object: tested it (not bare tested before…).

examples.said: before sending, publishing it to production
examples.correct: before pushing it to production / before deploying it to production

examples.said: push the production
examples.correct: push to production

items.rule: Collocation: push to production (with to). Not push the production; also prefer push/deploy over send/publish.

examples.said: the whole app went down
examples.correct: the whole checkout page went down

items.rule: Stay faithful to the story detail: checkout page, not the whole app.

examples.said: I would have rolled back the previous version
examples.correct: I would have rolled back to the previous version

items.rule: Roll back a deploy / roll back to a version (needs to before the version).

examples.said: But then this would not. This wouldn't have fixed the original bug
examples.correct: But that wouldn't have fixed the original bug

items.rule: Use that to refer back to the idea/action just mentioned (rolling back); avoid false-start this would not → this wouldn't.

examples.said: so I don't know
examples.correct: so I'm not sure

items.rule: For uncertainty about a judgment, I'm not sure often sounds more natural than I don't know.

examples.said: Maybe voice closer to mine
examples.correct: Maybe one closer to mine

items.rule: Need a determiner/pronoun before the adjective phrase: one closer to mine (not bare voice closer).

examples.said: and not sure if that's possible
examples.correct: but I'm not sure that's possible

items.rule: Keep the subject + verb: I'm not sure… (don't drop I'm). Prefer but over and for contrast.

examples.said: If not possible then just a male voice would be fine
examples.correct: If not, a male voice would be fine

items.rule: Shorter conditional: If not, … (drop possible then just).

examples.said: maybe (may-buh)
examples.correct: maybe /ˈmeɪbi/ with final /i/

items.rule: Keep the final /i/ in maybe — not schwa (may-buh).

examples.said: (monotone intonation across the utterance)
examples.correct: vary pitch — rise/fall on key words and at clause ends

items.rule: Azure flagged Monotone; practice pitch movement so statements and questions do not stay flat.

examples.said: Create a list of words I need to learn
examples.correct: Could you make a list of words I need to learn?

items.rule: Requests to the BOT sound more natural with Could you…? than a bare imperative Create…

examples.said: an when I would like to learn is spent on it
examples.correct: whenever I want to learn something new, I'll send it to you

items.rule: Don't use would after when for this habitual/future-plan meaning; use whenever + present (want), or I'll send…
items.notes: Lesson 4 answer (2026-10-22): whenever used correctly twice (pass).

examples.said: sentences or words or phrases
examples.correct: words, phrases, or whole sentences

items.rule: Natural order: words, phrases, or whole sentences (smaller → larger).

examples.said: world (meant word)
examples.correct: word /wɜːrd/ — no /l/

items.rule: word has no /l/; world has /l/. Don't add L to word.

examples.said: spent (heard spunt)
examples.correct: spent /spɛnt/ with /ɛ/ as in ten

items.rule: spent uses /ɛ/ (ten), not /ʌ/ (punt).

examples.said: an when… / you know
examples.correct: (pause) / drop filler or use um/so once

items.rule: Filler an… and you know while searching for words; pause silently instead when possible.

examples.said: But I am giving you an order
examples.correct: But I'm giving you an order

items.rule: In casual speech use I'm unless you are stressing am for emphasis.

examples.said: remember to not send
examples.correct: remember not to send

items.rule: After remember / try / decide, put not before to: remember not to… (not remember to not…).

examples.said: the new lesson
examples.correct: a new lesson

items.rule: Use a/an for a not-yet-specific item (a new lesson), not the.

examples.said: either quickly solved the bug or postpone deadline
examples.correct: either fix it quickly or postpone the deadline / push the deadline back

items.rule: After either…or, keep parallel base verbs (fix… or postpone…). Avoid mixing past solved with present postpone.

examples.said: right before deadline
examples.correct: right before a deadline

examples.said: postpone deadline
examples.correct: postpone the deadline

items.rule: Countable deadline usually needs an article: a deadline / the deadline.

examples.said: whenever you find a bug… you find a way…
examples.correct: Whenever I find a bug… I either fix it…

items.rule: When asked what you do (about yourself), answer with I, not a general you — unless you mean people in general on purpose.

examples.said: Keep your commentaries short and succinct
examples.correct: Keep your comments short and succinct

items.rule: commentary is for sports/news analysis; feedback remarks are comments.

examples.said: if you explained in using audio understand
examples.correct: if you explained them in audio, I'd understand

items.rule: Second conditional: if + past, would + base verb. Keep the object them after explain.

examples.said: succinct (/-sɪnt/, K dropped)
examples.correct: succinct /səkˈsɪŋkt/ — end like sink + T (suck-SINKT)

items.rule: Keep the /ŋk/ cluster before final /t/: -SINKT, not -sint. Second attempt was correct (94).

examples.said: every time that his boss asks for a new change
examples.correct: because his manager has rejected every version (four times / over the last three weeks)

items.rule: Stay faithful to the story reason and key details (rejected every version; four times; over the last three weeks).

examples.said: using crockpot
examples.correct: using a crock pot

items.rule: Singular countable nouns usually need a/an: a crock pot.

examples.said: what I changed in my routine I started using crockpot
examples.correct: One thing I've changed in my routine is that I've started using a crock pot

items.rule: Don't leave a what-clause dangling before a new subject+verb. Use One thing I've changed is that…
